text:
oliver_fin: Orbit Partners pinged us: their April settlement shows a short of 14 instance-hours vs our payable. They attached marketplace CSV and our ledger excerpt. Can billing validate?

maya_billing: pulling their marketplace report and our import now. any partner invoice id?

fern_partners: invoice OP-APR-26-09. Partner pasted this snippet in portal: 
```
sku,usage_start,usage_end,units,timezone
redwood-inference.standard,2026-04-05T23:00:00Z,2026-04-06T00:00:00Z,14,UTC+1
```
They say the 14 units are present in AWS but missing from our ledger.

ingest-bot: deploy: billing-ingest v3.2.0 rolled out 2026-04-06T01:10:02Z.

maya_billing: raw marketplace file includes the 14-unit row. Our import CSV (reseller_payable) does not. Import log shows "info: row normalized to local-day 2026-04-06 then dropped by day-window filter".

oliver_fin: day-window filter? explain.

maya_billing: our settlement runs aggregate by partner local-day. v3.2.0 changed timezone normalization to prefer partner timezone tag if present, but then our day-window filter compared against UTC boundaries. For partners in UTC+1 the row shifted to the next local day and failed the month-day inclusion check for the April 5 window. In short: we normalized to local-day but applied UTC boundaries when deciding which billing period to include.

fern_partners: partner says they set timezone in portal UTC+1 so they expected local-day aggregation. They included the row in their uploaded settlement exactly as above.

jess_treasury: what's the $$ impact? If we missed 14 instance-hours at April rate, we need a credit or corrected invoice.

maya_billing: unit price April = $300/hr. 14 * 300 = $4,200.

oliver_fin: propose: (1) issue $4,200 credit note to Orbit Partners (or reissue invoice per their preference), (2) backfill ledger for Apr 5/6 with corrected aggregation, (3) patch ingest to ensure timezone normalization and billing-window checks use the same base (either all UTC or all partner-local), (4) add test for timezone edge rows.

fern_partners: partner prefers corrected invoice rather than separate credit. They said it helps their reconciliation.

maya_billing: ok will regenerate invoice OP-APR-26-09-rev1 and re-run ledger import. Running backfill now. ETA ~15m.

ingest-bot: backfill job started: backfill-id bf-2026-04-06-5521.

jess_treasury: pre-approve adjustment of $4,200 pending import results and partner confirmation. Mark FIN-3699 created when backfill completes.

maya_billing: backfill complete. s3://redwood-billing/reconciliations/2026-04-orbit-backfill.csv import id imp-2026-04-06-5521. Ledger shows the 14 units now. I attached revised invoice draft to FIN-3699.

fern_partners: partner acknowledged the revised invoice and prefers we void original and send rev1. They also requested a short note explaining the root cause.

oliver_fin: summary for FIN-3699: billing-ingest v3.2.0 introduced inconsistent timezone handling: rows were normalized to partner-local day but billing-period inclusion checks used UTC boundaries, causing a small set of boundary rows to be dropped. Impact: Orbit Partners, 14 units = $4,200. Remediation: regenerated invoice (rev1), backfilled ledger, patched ingest to unify timezone base (now partner-local for both normalization and window checks), added unit/integration tests for timezone edges, and added alert when "day-boundary drops" >0.

jess_treasury: treasury note: will process corrected invoice in next AP run. FIN-3699 marked approved for payment adjustment.

maya_billing: will attach post-deploy test results and unit test IDs to the FIN ticket.

oliver_fin: thanks team. leaving thread open until AP confirms payment and controller signs off GL entries. :white_check_mark:
